source: Future Radio — The Artup Production Plan, v0.1 (2026-10-27)

episodes.title: The First Transmission
episodes.logline: Leonardo builds Future Radio to get funding from the future so he can finish his work.

episodes.title: The People vs. The Future
episodes.logline: A premortem disguised as a press conference at Milliways. Agnolo puts the season's plan on trial before it has been made.

scenes.title: The Transmission Arrives
scenes.summary: Leonardo's message reaches the future. Agnolo discovers the reply is a pitch deck and an invitation to Milliways.
scenes.question: What did Leonardo's original investment actually create?

scenes.title: Are We on Episode 2 or 10?
scenes.summary: Yuria announces Episode 10 as the second broadcast. The ending arrives before the middle.
scenes.question: Can an ending serve as a production plan?

scenes.title: Roll Call Across Centuries
scenes.summary: Shannon, Gödel, Hayek, Borges, Douglas, Leonardo, and the Creator identify their era and question.
scenes.question: Which expert perspectives are actually needed?

scenes.title: The Venture Capital Misunderstanding
scenes.summary: Agnolo displays the historical article, highlights a pitch-deck subject, and summons it as a witness.
scenes.question: What was promised, and what has actually happened?

scenes.title: Slide Six's Future Profits
scenes.summary: A projection claims that costs and time will fall while receipts rise. Agnolo refuses to book future outcomes as cash.
scenes.question: What would count as evidence of profitability?

scenes.title: The Angel Investor Mix-Up
scenes.summary: A Renaissance merchant, investors, and literal angels disagree about the meaning of a return.
scenes.question: What kinds of value can patrons and investors receive?

scenes.title: The Artist Inside the Founder
scenes.summary: Agnolo discovers the first artist using the artup is its founder. Leonardo recognizes the problem of unfinished ideas.
scenes.question: Who is this technology meant to serve?

scenes.title: Patrick's $250 Challenge
scenes.summary: The paid $1,000 engagement meets the unresolved $250/month value test. Marvin's capabilities go on trial.
scenes.question: What would make ongoing service valuable enough to renew?

scenes.title: Summon Failure
scenes.summary: Agnolo summons failure from November 30. Perfectionism, nobody listening, hidden labor, empty treasury, and overwhelming success testify.
scenes.question: What could prevent the season from finishing?

scenes.title: The Writers' Room Appears
scenes.summary: The screen enters a writers' room. Borges recalls prior ideas, Leonardo helps a patron make something, and Agnolo accounts for it.
scenes.question: Can patrons participate in real creative decisions?

scenes.title: Before It Exists
scenes.summary: An ensemble satirizes the demand to account for consequences before exploration is permitted.
scenes.question: What can responsibly be known before an experiment?

scenes.title: Leonardo Learns Project Management
scenes.summary: Leonardo chooses eight episodes, four rounds, deadlines, budgets, selection rules, and a definition of done.
scenes.question: How can the artist finish without abandoning imagination?

scenes.title: Enough Time
scenes.summary: The melody of Not Enough Time returns, transformed from regret about unfinished work into an acceptance of choosing.
scenes.question: Can finishing something be a creative achievement?

scenes.title: The Second Press Conference
scenes.summary: Agnolo announces another press conference on the same episode, this time treating it as the season finale.
scenes.question: How does interpretation change with context?

scenes.title: A Song That Doesn't Exist Yet
scenes.summary: A listener requests an unwritten song. Yuria invites them to describe it. The season's missing middle begins.
scenes.question: Can the audience help create the next transmission?

scenes.title: Who Is Dennis?
scenes.summary: Agnolo finds an unresolved name in the old pitch documentation and adds it to the ledger.
scenes.question: Which mysteries should remain open?

ideas.title: Six-sequence cut for Episode 10
ideas.question: Can the ten selected scenes compress into six sequences producible in one day?
ideas.reason: Core selection is larger than one day allows; a complete 8–12 minute cut beats a partial 25-minute one.
ideas.note: 1 Arrival at Milliways · 2 The Pitch Deck on Trial · 3 The Founder on Trial · 4 The Premortem · 5 Leonardo's Decision · 6 The Invitation

ideas.title: The full Angel Investor sequence
ideas.question: What kinds of value can patrons and investors receive?
ideas.reason: Saved for later unless it can be produced with negligible incremental effort.

ideas.title: The expert roll call across centuries
ideas.question: Which expert perspectives are actually needed?
ideas.reason: Most of the roll call is saved for later; Episode 10 keeps only the characters it needs.

ideas.title: Before It Exists (ensemble song)
ideas.question: What can responsibly be known before an experiment?
ideas.reason: Longer musical numbers are saved for later to keep tomorrow's cut feasible.

ideas.title: Enough Time (reprise of Not Enough Time)
ideas.question: Can finishing something be a creative achievement?
ideas.reason: Longer musical numbers are saved for later; a strong candidate for the season's final round.

ideas.title: Who Is Dennis?
ideas.question: Which mysteries should remain open?
ideas.reason: Post-credits mystery kept open in the ledger for a later episode.

ideas.title: The Second Press Conference (Episode 10 as finale)
ideas.question: Which missing events, character changes and real-world outcomes would make Episode 10 meaningful as a finale?
ideas.note: Planned for Oct 29–31; becomes the creative brief for November.

forecasts.claim: Solo mode can produce one compact episode per day.
A compact episode can be produced within a $20 cash ceiling.
Episode 10 ships tomorrow as a complete 8–12 minute audio-first cut.
The artup shows receipts minus attributable costs above zero for November, with founder labor and historical investment disclosed.
Client feedback: the AI is not yet worth $250/month. Test: the service becomes worth $250/month, ideally shown by a paid renewal.
